proposed_from.topic: Pointwise CATE benchmark-rate achievability under a fixed positive-band unknown design density: construct a total close-pair local R-estimator attaining the Kennedy--Balakrishnan--Robins--Wasserman rate on a nonempty smoothness region without density estimation or density smoothness, while leaving the exact band-only minimax exponent and matching positive-band converse open.
proposed_from.novelty_justification: The core preserves a fixed positive density lower bound, derives an estimator-independent lower branch of polynomial order n^{-(alpha+beta)/d}, matches that exponent with a primitive-class rank-capped estimator, and proves polynomial separation from the KBRW benchmark on a nonempty open low-smoothness region. Existing empirical and stabilized HOIF results do not cover the required beyond-rank localized regime.

seed_details.title: Band-only density minimax slowdown

anchor_paper.opened_sections: Introduction; Theorem 1 and its density remark; Remark 8; Discussion

seed_details.open_question_leveraged: Determine whether weaker covariate-distribution conditions change the pointwise CATE minimax rate.
seed_details.claim_kernel: Over a fixed two-sided density band, prove a density-coupled lower branch \(n^{-(\alpha+\beta)/d}\), match its polynomial exponent, and show strict separation from \(r_n^{\mathrm{KBRW}}\) on an open low-smoothness region.
seed_details.cynical_referee_objection: Immediate from Kennedy (2023), because its undersmoothed local R-learner already has the \(n^{-(\alpha+\beta)/d}\) error term.
seed_details.rebuttal: Kennedy (2023) proves only an estimator upper bound and calls its minimax optimality a deepest open question; the density-coupled lower bound over one primitive positive-density class is new.
seed_details.closest_result_and_gap: Kennedy et al. (2024) obtain \(r_n^{\mathrm{KBRW}}\) only with density-qualified attainment and do not prove any band-only slowdown.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The claim is uniform over a relatively open smoothness region and rests on mixture indistinguishability, not on one singular Gram matrix or one hand-tuned law.
seed_details.burned_reason: The selected strict band-only slowdown angle collapsed: KBRW cancellation relies on support holes, and no valid fixed-positive-band converse was obtained.

seed_details.title: Localized Gram rank phase transition
seed_details.open_question_leveraged: Extend stabilized HOIF theory to \(k\gtrsim n\) and determine how density regularity enters.
seed_details.claim_kernel: Derive a necessary-and-sufficient threshold in \(k/(nh^d)\) for equivalence between population-Gram and density-free localized HOIF estimators.
seed_details.cynical_referee_objection: This is only the elementary rank condition \(k<nh^d\).
seed_details.rebuttal: Invertibility is elementary, but an estimator-independent divergence frontier requires matching risk bounds and counterexamples after localization and same-sample self-normalization.
seed_details.closest_result_and_gap: Liu et al. (2026) analyze global bilinear forms for \(k=o(n)\), not bandwidth-dependent local CATE moments or the necessity side.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The seed names a derived observable scaling frontier and both equivalence and divergence directions.

seed_details.title: Proportional-rank stabilized local HOIF limit

anchor_paper.opened_sections: Introduction; main estimator construction; Theorem 1; Concluding Remarks

seed_details.open_question_leveraged: Establish statistical guarantees for regularized Gram inversion in the proportional regime.
seed_details.claim_kernel: Derive the nonstandard limit law of a same-sample stabilized localized HOIF CATE estimator when \(k/(nh^d)\to\rho\in(0,1)\).
seed_details.cynical_referee_objection: Liu et al. (2026) already prove asymptotic normality for stabilized HOIF estimators.
seed_details.rebuttal: Their theorem has \(k=o(n)\) for global bilinear forms; proportional local rank changes both self-normalization and the dominant degenerate component.
seed_details.closest_result_and_gap: Robins et al. (2016) treat deterministic changing kernels, while Liu et al. (2026) treat same-sample random Gram matrices without localization.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The limit distribution is the headline rather than an assumed CLT.

seed_details.title: Shrinking-functional efficiency frontier
seed_details.open_question_leveraged: Develop inference beyond bias and variance for the localized CATE statistic.
seed_details.claim_kernel: Characterize the semiparametric efficiency bound for the smoothed projection CATE \(\tau_h(x_0)\) as \(h\downarrow0\).
seed_details.cynical_referee_objection: The influence function of a fixed-bandwidth weighted projection follows from standard pathwise differentiation.
seed_details.rebuttal: The objection holds: without a new uniform shrinking-bandwidth lower bound, this would be a routine calculation rather than a frontier result.
seed_details.closest_result_and_gap: KBRW already define the weighted projection; the missing step is limit theory, not a fixed-\(h\) efficiency calculation.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: Search obstruction for the required M11(b) lane: the credible fixed-functional object collapses to standard semiparametric calculus.

seed_details.title: Honest CATE interval length under band-only design

anchor_paper.opened_sections: Introduction; overall-rate theorem; Discussion on inference

seed_details.open_question_leveraged: Obtain the distribution and honest inference theory for the pointwise CATE estimator.
seed_details.claim_kernel: Derive uniform coverage and minimax expected length for a bias-aware pointwise CATE interval under band-only design.
seed_details.cynical_referee_objection: Armstrong and Koles\'ar (2020) already solve honest pointwise intervals.
seed_details.rebuttal: Their scalar regression statistic has neither nuisance-product bias nor a random localized higher-order projection operator.
seed_details.closest_result_and_gap: Robins et al. (2016) provide changing-kernel U-statistic CLTs, but not uniform bias-aware coverage with an unsmooth random design law.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The interval-length lower bound and derived limit law are first-class objects; asymptotic normality is not assumed.

seed_details.title: Adaptation across density regularity classes

anchor_paper.opened_sections: Introduction; density qualification; Discussion on adaptivity

seed_details.open_question_leveraged: Select bandwidth and projection dimension when nuisance and design regularities are unknown.
seed_details.claim_kernel: Construct a Lepski selector across band-only and H\"older-density classes and prove the sharp adaptation penalty.
seed_details.cynical_referee_objection: This is a routine Lepski wrapper around the KBRW estimator.
seed_details.rebuttal: The candidate risks change active stochastic branches and Gram rank, so the selector must compare nonnested higher-order statistics; nevertheless the base band-only rate must be settled first.
seed_details.closest_result_and_gap: Chichignoud and Lederer (2014) adapt ordinary pointwise regression to weak design assumptions but have no causal nuisance interaction or projection dimension.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The seed includes a sharp adaptation-cost lower bound, not only a data-driven tuning rule.

seed_details.title: Local treatment-choice regret at the density bottleneck

anchor_paper.opened_sections: Introduction on treatment allocation; Theorem 1; Discussion

seed_details.open_question_leveraged: Translate pointwise CATE limits into optimal treatment allocation under local covariate constraints.
seed_details.claim_kernel: Derive minimax welfare regret for a policy class that can change treatment only in a shrinking neighborhood of \(x_0\).
seed_details.cynical_referee_objection: For one local decision, regret is a direct margin-weighted corollary of pointwise CATE estimation.
seed_details.rebuttal: The objection holds for the natural policy class; no independent policy-complexity frontier remains after conditioning on the CATE rate.
seed_details.closest_result_and_gap: The anchor motivates allocation but does not supply a nontrivial local policy class whose regret is distinct from sign estimation.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: Search obstruction for the required M16 lane: the credible pointwise policy loss mechanically reduces to the fixed-estimand error.

seed_details.title: Permutation inversion for pointwise CATE
seed_details.open_question_leveraged: Construct uncertainty quantification for pointwise CATE without relying on a standard Wald limit.
seed_details.claim_kernel: Invert a local treatment-label permutation test to obtain a confidence set for \(\tau_P(x_0)\).
seed_details.cynical_referee_objection: Observational unconfoundedness does not create a finite-sample treatment-label symmetry conditional on a continuously valued \(X\).
seed_details.rebuttal: The objection holds: imposing the required exchangeability orbit would strengthen the design beyond the band-only observational model and change the question.
seed_details.closest_result_and_gap: No anchor supplies the exact group action needed for M17; asymptotic local randomization would return to an M11(c) problem.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: Search obstruction for the required M17 lane: the symmetry needed for exact inversion is absent from the maintained observational model.

proposed_from.literature_map: Chosen candidate S1. Settled: Kennedy et al. (2024, Theorem 1) derive the KBRW localized fuzzy-hypothesis lower rate, and their upper theorem attains it only under an explicit covariate-law estimation condition; the remark after Theorem 1 and Remark 8 identify density as future work. Settled: Kennedy (2023, Corollary 3) proves an undersmoothed local R-learner upper rate with polynomial branch \(n^{-(\alpha+\beta)/d}\) and explicitly leaves minimax optimality open. Settled: Liu et al. (2017, Theorem 2) remove density smoothness for global empirical HOIFs with projection dimension below sample size. Settled: Liu et al. (2026, Theorem 1) stabilize same-sample Gram inversion for global bilinear forms with \(k=o(n)\), and Concluding Remark 1 leaves \(k\gtrsim n\) and density-dependent regularization open. Adjacent method: Shen et al. (2020, Sections 2--3) obtain random-design regression-functional upper and lower bounds without design-density smoothness using pairwise U-statistics and sparse allocation. No closer published paper found in searches through August 2026 establishes a lower bound over a fixed two-sided-banded density class, a localized rank threshold for CATE, or a strict polynomial separation from the KBRW benchmark. Candidate S2 remains viable but is estimator-frontier rather than estimand-frontier. Candidate S5 remains viable but depends on first resolving the band-only point-estimation scale. The M11(b), M16, and M17 lanes were searched and dropped for the specific obstructions recorded in S4, S7, and S8.
